channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lira e Gaspar selam aliança e lançam chapa ao Senado por Alagoas
item.description: Deputies Arthur Lira (PP-AL) and Alfredo Gaspar (PL-AL) announced a joint Senate ticket for Alagoas in 2026, coordinated by PL, PP and União Brasil to counter Senator Renan Calheiros (MDB) and prevent opposition vote splitting. The alliance follows Gaspar’s national rise from leading the INSS CPMI probe and aims to unite opposition forces against the Calheiros political bloc in the state.

item.title: Haddad diz que Tarcísio “namora a extrema direita”
item.description: Haddad stated that Tarcísio de Freitas 'is flirting with the far right', though he does not label him a fascist, citing his support for Trump's tariffs and laughter at Bolsonaro's anti-vaccine jokes. He criticized the governor's silence on the January 8 events and the military dictatorship, questioning his courage to speak out. Haddad positioned himself as a pre-candidate for the São Paulo gubernatorial race in 2026.

item.title: Gleisi Hoffmann perde ação contra Flávio por vídeo no Instagram
item.description: Federal deputy Gleisi Hoffmann lost her lawsuit against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for moral damages after he posted an Instagram video associating her with criminality. Judge Acácia Regina Soares de Sá ruled all claims unfounded, determining the post was a lawful political critique protected by freedom of speech and parliamentary immunity. Hoffmann was ordered to cover Flávio’s legal costs and attorney fees, set at 10% of the case’s value.

item.title: Por minutos, Flávio Bolsonaro e Zema não se encontram em evento
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro and Romeu Zema did not meet at an agribusiness event in Belo Horizonte due to a mere minutes-long difference in their arrival and departure, despite being invited to the same panel. Zema’s advisors denied intentionality, calling it an accidental coincidence. Ronaldo Caiado was also present, arriving while Bolsonaro participated in the panel and remaining during Zema’s appearance.

item.title: Esquerda questiona uso de camisa da seleção da Colômbia como símbolo político
item.description: Left-wing presidential candidate Iván Cepeda accused far-right rival Abelardo de la Espriella of improperly appropriating Colombia's national football jersey as a political symbol, drawing parallels to Jair Bolsonaro's use of Brazil's jersey in Brazil. Cepeda claimed the jersey had been 'stolen' and criticized its politicization for undermining national sentiment around football ahead of the 2026 World Cup. The race heads to a runoff on June 21, after Espirriella secured 43.7% in the first round versus Cepeda's 40.9%.

item.title: Mudança de humor na direita fortalece Caiado e Zema em cenários contra Lula em pesquisa
item.description: The Realtime Big Data poll shows Lula leading in the first round with 38%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 31%, while Caiado and Zema emerge as the most competitive opponents in a potential runoff, either tying or narrowly trailing Lula. Right-wing voters appear to favor candidates who uphold conservative rhetoric but are untainted by corruption scandals, which explains the strengthened positioning of Caiado and Zema.

item.title: Trump escolhe embaixador para o Brasil em meio a disputa com Lula sobre facções e Pix e tarifas
item.description: Donald Trump has nominated Daniel Perez as the new U.S. ambassador to Brazil, ending a diplomatic vacancy of over 16 months. The nomination comes amid rising tensions, following the U.S. designation of Brazil’s PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations — a move rejected by Lula as an infringement on national sovereignty. The dispute has expanded to include the Brazilian Pix payment system, which the U.S. is investigating under Section 301 for alleged anti-competitive practices, potentially opening the door to economic sanctions or tariffs against the system.

item.title: Flávio quer base de governo com quórum para mudar Constituição e defende menos ministérios
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, presidential pre-candidate and senator from PL-RJ, stated he aims to build a right-wing majority in Congress with sufficient quorum to approve constitutional changes, allied with the current president. He said this would allow institutions to return to operating within their limits. He also advocated for reducing the number of ministries.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que Haddad é o “melhor ministro da Fazenda da história do Paraguai”
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) criticized Fernando Haddad's tenure as Minister of Finance, claiming it led to economic deterioration, rising public debt, and the migration of Brazilian companies to Paraguay. He sarcastically called Haddad the 'best finance minister in Paraguay's history,' implying his policies favored Paraguay over Brazil.

item.title: Lula pede a Durigan que avalie possíveis prejuízos de medidas dos EUA
item.description: President Lula asked Finance Minister Dario Durigan to assess the potential harms of U.S. measures labeling CV and PCC as terrorist organizations on Brazilian companies and banks. Durigan emphasized concerns over the discretionary nature of the Trump administration's actions threatening Brazil's economic sovereignty and stressed the need to avoid unfounded sanctions. He also said he remains open to speaking with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent once a clear diagnosis is available.

item.title: "O caminho do precipício está visível", diz Domingos Sávio em Minas
item.description: Federal deputy Domingos Sávio (PL-MG) stated that Brazil is on a very visible path to a precipice, criticizing the increase in taxes and public debt under the Lula government, which he calls irresponsible. He emphasized that, alongside Flávio Bolsonaro and allies like Ronaldo Caiado, he feels responsible for promoting a deep change in the country, arguing that Congress has acted as a 'goalkeeper' trying to block harmful government initiatives, especially against rural producers.

item.title: Tarcísio sobe o tom e diz que Haddad é 'o melhor ministro da Fazenda da história do Paraguai'
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas mocked Fernando Haddad by calling him 'the best finance minister in Paraguay's history', claiming Brazil's high tax burden is driving companies to the neighboring country. He reiterated his 2026 re-election bid, criticized alleged Brazilian subservience to the U.S., and reaffirmed his support for Flávio Bolsonaro as presidential candidate, dismissing a third way due to polarization.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro defende que corte de gastos não pode afetar os mais vulneráveis
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, defended in Belo Horizonte the need to cut public spending, but stressed that such measures must not affect the most vulnerable, especially retirees and the elderly. He criticized the Lula government's indebtedness, noting that the debt-to-GDP ratio exceeded 80%, and proposed balancing public accounts through efficiency in the public machine, not through cuts to social policies such as health, education, or the minimum wage adjustment linked to retirees.

item.title: Justiça manda rede social remover publicações feitas com IA sobre Magno Malta
item.description: Judge Miguel Ferrari Júnior of São Paulo’s 43rd Civil Court ordered Facebook to remove within five days AI-generated posts allegedly damaging the honor of Senator Magno Malta (PL-ES), under threat of fines. The defense claims the images were intended to spread false narratives about an incident where Malta was accused of assaulting a nursing technician at Brasília’s DF Star Hospital. The ruling also mandates preservation of user access logs and registration data.

item.title: Ministro da Fazenda diz que governo tem preocupação com eventuais novas tarifas dos EUA
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan said the Lula government is concerned about potential new unilateral tariffs by the U.S. on Brazilian goods under Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act, citing investigations into deforestation and the Pix payment system. He also stated Brazil will engage with U.S. authorities to clarify the designation of PCC and CV as terrorist groups, calling the move an attempt to create instability ahead of elections.

item.title: Caiado cita filha de Silvio Santos como possível vice
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado suggested that Silvia Abravanel, daughter of Silvio Santos and a member of the PSD party, could be a potential running mate in his 2026 presidential bid. The comment was made during a press conference in Belo Horizonte on Monday, June 1st.

item.title: Haddad diz que escolha de vice dependerá de resolução de impasse sobre Senado; Lula prefere França
item.description: Fernando Haddad said his choice of running mate will depend on resolving the Senate impasse involving Márcio França, Simone Tebet, and Marina Silva, noting that Lula prefers França as vice, though the PSB wants to keep him as a Senate candidate. Haddad criticized Tarcísio de Freitas for attacking his economic policies and announced a three-pillar security plan targeting organized crime, territorial intelligence, and violence against vulnerable groups.

item.title: O Brasil que muita gente conhece, mas o ‘Dark Horse’ dos Bolsonaro não conta
item.description: Investigations reveal the diversion of parliamentary amendments and public funds linked to the film 'Dark Horse', involving Deputy Mário Frias (PL), the NGO Instituto Conhecer Brasil led by Karina Ferreira da Gama, and the production company Go Up, with suspicions of shell companies and overpriced contracts. The São Paulo City Hall also allocated over R$ 100 million to the same NGO for installing Wi-Fi points that were never implemented. Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro are connected to the project, having requested funds from Banco Master and the U.S., respectively.

item.title: Haddad diz que apoio de Tarcísio a Trump é “ataque ao Brasil”
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) criticized São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) for supporting the U.S. designation of the PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations, calling it an 'attack on Brazil' with economic consequences for financial institutions and businesses. Haddad also accused Tarcísio of undermining the Public Security PEC through his former secretary Guilherme Derrite.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro defende combate ao crime em visita a Minas
item.description: Senator and presidential pré-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) defended the fight against organized crime during a visit to Belo Horizonte, citing the police operation against PCC and CV in Minas Gerais. He stated the action is essential to free society from fear and urged Minas Gerais residents to help combat what he called 'terrorists'. Bolsonaro also received the title of Honorary Citizen of Belo Horizonte and referenced his recent meeting with Donald Trump, where public security was the central topic.

item.title: PT pede para investigar se há elo de aliados de Flávio com CV
item.description: Deputy Alencar Santana (PT-SP) filed a formal complaint with the Federal Police requesting an investigation into alleged links between allies of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and members of the Comando Vermelho. The document cites messages obtained in PF investigations indicating negotiations involving public office appointments, requests for favors, and articulations with public agents, including former Secretary Gutemberg Fonseca (‘Guto’), described as a close political ally of the senator. It also mentions Gabriel Dias de Oliveira (‘Índio do Lixão’), Luiz Eduardo Cunha Gonçalves (‘Dudu’), Alessandro Pitombeira Carracena, and others linked to influence-peddling schemes benefiting organized crime.

item.title: Lindbergh aciona STF para investigar ONG ligada ao “Dark Horse”
item.description: Federal Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) filed a petition with the STF requesting an investigation into an alleged scheme involving the diversion of public funds through a R$108 million contract between São Paulo City Hall and Instituto Conhecer Brasil, an NGO linked to businesswoman Karina Ferreira da Gama, who also controls the producer of the Dark Horse film about Jair Bolsonaro. The petition, based on a São Paulo Civil Police inquiry, cites suspicions of bidding fraud, asset commingling between the NGO and film producer, and possible money laundering via parliamentary amendments.

item.title: Renan Santos diz que “arrasará” Lula em debates de 1º e 2º turno
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for president from the Missão party, claimed in a social media video that he will 'crush' Lula in the first and second round debates, citing a Real Time Big Data poll placing him third with 6% voter intention, despite saying he does not trust the institute's methodology. He also reaffirmed hardline security policies, stating he wants to 'kill criminals as if there were no tomorrow,' and aims to make Brazil one of the world's top five nations within 30 years.

item.title: Camisa da seleção entra na guerra política da Colômbia
item.description: In Colombia, presidential candidate Abelardo de la Espriella was accused by rival Iván Cepeda of politicizing the yellow jersey of the Colombian national team by wearing it during campaign events, drawing parallels to the political use of Brazil’s jersey by Bolsonaro supporters. The Colombian Football Federation urged that the sports symbol be kept out of electoral politics. Both candidates lead the first round and will face off in a runoff on June 21.

item.title: Frias e Flávio defendem produtora de ‘Dark Horse’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and federal deputy Mário Frias defended the production company Go UP, responsible for the film 'Dark Horse', after the Civil Police launched an operation against the Instituto Conhecer Brasil, linked to businesswoman Karina Gama, a partner in the producer. The action investigates suspicions of fraud in public funds, but the parliamentarians claimed the initiative is political and aims to attack the image of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Brasil não pode ser vassalo dos EUA, diz Durigan sobre PCC e CV
item.description: Finance Minister Dario Durigan stated that Brazil should not accept a vassal-like position vis-à-vis the United States, criticizing the unilateral designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations by the U.S. government. He warned that the move could increase compliance costs for banks and fintechs, raise tariffs, trigger financial sanctions, and threaten the Pix payment system, which symbolizes Brazil’s financial sovereignty. Durigan emphasized Brazil’s willingness to share information but rejected yielding autonomy under U.S. pressure.

item.title: Tarcísio diz que Bolsonaro foi “extremamente injustiçado”
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas revealed that former President Jair Bolsonaro discussed with him, on more than one occasion, the possibility of a presidential candidacy for the Bolsonarist camp in 2026, but that he declined the offer. Tarcísio declared full support for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and stated that Bolsonaro was 'extremely unjustly treated', referring to the former president's convictions and ineligibility.

item.title: TCE rejeita contas do governo Cláudio Castro de 2025
item.description: The TCE-RJ rejected the 2025 government accounts of former Governor Cláudio Castro (PL) by a 3-1 vote, citing fiscal and budgetary irregularities, though the decision is not final and requires approval by the Alerj. Castro’s advisors denied the allegations, stating his accounts were consistently approved by the Court and that his administration upheld transparency and fiscal responsibility. The TCE-RJ’s rejection follows his 8-year ineligibility by the TSE in March 2026 for abuse of political and economic power in the 2022 campaign.

item.title: Aécio tem rejeição 15 vezes maior que intenções de voto, aponta RealTime
item.description: According to the Real Time Big Data poll, federal deputy Aécio Neves (PSDB) shows a rejection rate 15 times higher than his voting intentions, placing him among the only candidates with rejection above 40%, alongside Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). The data reveals a high level of public disapproval toward the tucano, despite his presence in the electoral landscape.

item.title: Polícia apreende HD com contratos da Prefeitura e celular de produtora do filme de Bolsonaro
item.description: São Paulo Civil Police executed search warrants at eight locations linked to an investigation into alleged fraud in a R$108 million contract between the Institute Conhecer Brasil (ICB) and the city hall for the WiFi Livre SP project. Authorities seized cell phones, laptops, USB drives, documents, and a hard drive containing contracts from the Municipal Secretariat of Innovation and Technology, including Karina Ferreira da Gama’s phone — she is a partner in the production company behind the Bolsonaro film 'Dark Horse'. Her defense has not responded; the city denies wrongdoing, citing legal compliance, while Mayor Ricardo Nunes calls the operation politically motivated.

item.title: Operação Wi-Fi: Flávio Bolsonaro diz esperar que 'parte' da Polícia de São Paulo não seja usada para 'fins eleitoreiros'
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) responded to Operation Wi-Fi by São Paulo's Civil Police, which investigates alleged misuse of public funds from the NGO Instituto Conhecer Brasil to finance the film 'Dark Horse', produced by a company linked to his family. He expressed hope that 'part' of the police force is not being used for electoral purposes and rejected claims of undergoing a 'fishing expedition' or persecution, stating the contract was fully fulfilled and predated the film's conception. The operation took place as Flávio intensifies his agenda in Minas Gerais to secure agribusiness support for the PL.

item.title: Investigações da PF sobre corrupção eleitoral disparam e crescem quase 20 vezes desde 2016
item.description: Federal Police investigations into electoral corruption grew nearly 20 times from 2016 to 2024, rising from 117 to 2,283 inquiries. Over the past decade, more than 7,600 investigations were launched — averaging two new cases per day — involving vote-buying through cash, goods, healthcare services, and job promises. The crime is concentrated in Brazil's interior and persists despite electoral modernization.

item.title: Aulas de português e goleada contra o Panamá: o caminho de Ancelotti para tentar 'conquistar o Brasil'
item.description: Carlo Ancelotti, the first foreign head coach of the Brazilian national team for the 2026 World Cup, is learning Portuguese with four weekly lessons to better connect with players and fans. His dedication to the language was praised by his tutor, Roberto Piantino, who noted Ancelotti’s willingness to attend lessons even on Saturdays. The effort aims to overcome Brazil’s traditional football self-sufficiency and build trust with the staff and public.

item.title: Papo Antagonista: Aécio Neves na corrida presidencial? Os planos do PSDB para as eleições
item.description: In the Papo Antagonista program, the presumed PSDB presidential candidate Aécio Neves discussed the party's plans for the 2026 elections. The interview addressed the feasibility of his candidacy and the PSDB's strategies to reposition itself in the national political landscape.

item.title: Petista pede à PF investigação sobre suposta ligação de Flávio com crime organizado
item.description: Federal deputy Alencar Santana (PT-SP) filed a formal complaint with the Federal Police requesting an investigation into alleged ties between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and the Red Command (CV). The document cites evidence suggesting CV members or intermediaries sought access, influence, appointments, and political protection. The request was submitted on April 1st and aims to investigate potential connections between the lawmaker and organized crime.

item.title: Especialistas defendem mudança na legislação e melhoria na fiscalização para evitar fake news nas eleições
item.description: Experts at a public hearing of the CCS in the National Congress advocated for updating legislation and strengthening oversight to combat fake news in the 2026 elections, particularly due to advances in generative AI. They warned that disinformation threatens the credibility of electronic voting machines and Brazil’s electoral system, undermining principles such as equal opportunity and popular sovereignty.

item.title: Proibidos no Brasil, Polymarket e Kalshi viralizam na direita como alternativa às pesquisas eleitorais
item.description: Prediction market platforms such as Polymarket and Kalshi, which are banned in Brazil, are gaining traction among right-wing Brazilian groups as alternatives to traditional electoral polls. Despite being promoted on social media as a barometer for the 2026 presidential race, experts warn these platforms are unreliable for forecasting election outcomes due to sampling biases and susceptibility to manipulation. Their growing use reflects declining trust in polling institutions and a preference for alternative indicators, even if methodologically flawed.

item.title: Áudio: Uso da IA é desafio na propaganda eleitoral de 2026, dizem especialistas
item.description: The National Congress's Social Communication Council debated the TSE's rules for online electoral propaganda, emphasizing the fight against disinformation as the main challenge amid rapid AI advancement. Experts warn that the use of AI tools in the 2026 electoral campaign requires new regulations to safeguard democratic integrity.

item.title: Tarcísio chama Haddad de 'ministro da Fazenda do Paraguai' e diz que nunca se reuniu com Vorcaro
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas criticized former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad by calling him the 'best finance minister in Paraguay's history,' implying his tax policies drove Brazilian industries to the neighboring country. He also denied ever meeting businessman Vorcaro, countering allegations of ties between the São Paulo government and private sector figures.

item.title: Vini Jr. tem maior valorização entre jogadores da seleção
item.description: Vini Jr. was the Brazilian national team player with the highest valuation increase from 2022 to 2026, rising from €100 million to €200 million, according to a Betfair study. The current squad is the most valuable in history, totaling €978.7 million. Conversely, Neymar experienced the largest devaluation, dropping from €90 million to €10 million.

item.title: Os números do PT que mostram a repercussão de ações de Lula e Flávio nas redes
item.description: PT officials say the approval of the PEC ending the 6×1 work schedule helped the government rebalance social media discourse after Flávio Bolsonaro’s U.S. trip generated positive traction. While the designation of Brazilian criminal groups as terrorist organizations drew 24.1 million interactions (66% favorable), the 6×1 PEC reached 42.3 million interactions (81% favorable), allowing the government to reclaim momentum with a popular labor agenda as a counterpoint to Bolsonaro’s security-focused narrative.

item.title: PSD mira eleitorado feminino em inserções, e senadora defende 'mão pesada' contra agressores
item.description: Senator Mara Gabrilli (PSD) reinforced in a party TV insertion the slogan of presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado, promising a 'heavy hand' against aggressors of women. The message aims to attract female voters with a focus on security and combating gender-based violence.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro fala em 'pescaria probatória' e 'perseguição' ao comentar operação contra ONG de produtora de 'Dark Horse'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and pre-candidate for president, commented in Belo Horizonte on the São Paulo Civil Police operation against the NGO Instituto Conhecer Brasil, linked to the producer of the film 'Dark Horse', calling it a 'probatory fishing expedition' and 'persecution'. He denied any irregularities in his relationship with former banker Vorcaro of Banco Master, despite leaked messages showing he requested funds for Jair Bolsonaro’s biopic. The visit included allies such as Nikolas Ferreira and Bruno Engler, and was marked by greetings to supporters of his pre-candidacy and of Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Em Lisboa, Kassab assegura candidatura de Caiado e prega fim de emendas
item.description: Gilberto Kassab, president of the PSD, advocated in Lisbon for mixed-district voting, government transparency, and parliamentary amendment reform, while reinforcing Ronaldo Caiado’s 2026 presidential candidacy as part of a third-way strategy.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Lula empata com Zema e Caiado em 2° turno, mas vence Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: In projections for the 2026 Brazilian elections, former president Lula ties with candidates Romeu Zema and Ronaldo Caiado in a potential runoff, but would defeat Flávio Bolsonaro if matched against him. The scenario reflects a highly polarized political landscape, with Lula maintaining strength against right-wing opponents while facing stronger competition from centrist and moderate right figures.

item.title: Proximidade com Mario Frias, moradora da periferia, filme sobre Bolsonaro: quem é Karina Gama, alvo de operação policial em SP
item.description: Karina Ferreira da Gama, a resident of Brasilândia in São Paulo and producer of the film 'Dark Horse' about Jair Bolsonaro, had her home address, the headquarters of her NGO Instituto Conhecer Brasil, and her production company Go Up Entertainment targeted in a police search and seizure operation by São Paulo’s Civil Police investigating alleged irregularities in contracts with Mayor Ricardo Nunes’ administration. Her close ties to federal deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP), including providing press advisory for his campaign and securing parliamentary amendments that benefited her NGO, have drawn scrutiny. She also established holdings in Aracaju and is a partner in a Salvador-based construction firm, having secured major public contracts, including R$ 108 million for installing public Wi-Fi hotspots.

item.title: Os efeitos perversos da decisão dos EUA sobre a economia brasileira
item.description: The U.S. designation of PCC and CV as terrorist organizations may undermine police cooperation against organized crime by reclassifying useful intelligence as sensitive and secret, hindering investigations and judicial proceedings. The measure could also serve as a geopolitical coercion tool, enabling the U.S. Treasury to impose terrorism-related sanctions on Brazilian banks, companies, and exporters, potentially disrupting the national financial system and threatening sovereignty. The timing of the announcement—two days after Flávio Bolsonaro’s visit to Trump—raises concerns about electoral interference.

item.title: PT fará pesquisa para decidir candidato do partido ao governo de MG
item.description: The PT will begin internal polling this week to determine its candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, following Senator Rodrigo Pacheco's (PSB) withdrawal from the race. The move aims to secure a strong electoral base for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Brazil's second-largest state, after Pacheco's departure created a leadership vacuum.

item.title: Eleições 2026: União já disponibilizou ao TSE recursos do Fundo Eleitoral
item.description: The federal government has made available to the TSE the R$ 4.9 billion from the Special Campaign Financing Fund (FEFC) for the 2026 General Elections, meeting the legal deadline of June 1. The funds will be distributed to parties based on legal criteria, including performance in the last Chamber of Deputies elections and number of elected representatives in Congress. Parties may renounce the funds, provided they formally notify the TSE by June 1.

item.title: Zema é notificado em processo por calúnia movido por Gilmar Mendes e diz que não vai se calar
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) was notified by Federal Justice in a defamation lawsuit filed by Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes, following satirical videos linking Mendes to the Master case. Zema declared he will not be silenced and will continue exposing what he calls 'absurdities' in Brazil, despite having 15 days to respond to the notification.
